review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked the likely candidates for a competing concept: IsCompleteBetween, IsIsolated, IsUniversal, completeBipartiteGraph, completeGraph/emptyGraph, support, edgeSetEmbedding/edgeSet, fromRel, fromEdgeSet, and incidenceSet. I grepped Mathlib for other definitions of these concepts.

- IsCompleteBetween, IsIsolated and IsUniversal have no independent Mathlib counterpart. Other files (Star, Maps, Finite, UniversalVerts, Tutte) build on them.
- completeBipartiteGraph is a different concept from completeMultipartiteGraph. Several files use it, including Maps and Zarankiewicz.
- support already goes through SetRel.dom, and edgeSetEmbedding already reuses Sym2.fromRel.
- fromRel and fromEdgeSet are named specialisations with distinct semantics.
- completeGraph and emptyGraph are abbreviations for ⊤ and ⊥. They are intentional named aliases, so I did not treat them as competing versions.

I found no independent competing declaration with a concrete cost, so I abstained. The one remaining uncertainty is that IsCompleteBetween could in principle be phrased through a product-set/SetRel containment. I found no existing Mathlib predicate for it, so I did not report it.
